title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Month Count Where Booked Visits Went Unattended
content:
## Service coordinator note

The months a charge for instalments left unpaid is counted for, on a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record, are reduced where the office itself failed to attend. The reading is taken from the preventive visits booked on the agreement against the preventive visits completed on it.

### The rule

- Where **2 or more** booked preventive visits of the agreement stand with no preventive visit completed against them, the charge is counted for a single month only.
- Where **exactly 1** booked preventive visit stands with no preventive visit completed against it, the count of whole months completed since the anchor day is taken and never falls below one month.
- Where **every** booked preventive visit has been answered by a completed preventive visit, the months the charge is counted for run from the day the most recent instalment invoice fell due to the day the charge is raised, each month and each part month counting as a whole month.

The anchor day is the day the most recent instalment invoice fell due.

### Cases (hypothetical)

| Booked preventive visits standing with no preventive visit completed against them | Whole months completed since the anchor day | Months the charge is counted for |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 4 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 4 | 4 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 |
| none | 2 whole months and a part month | 3 |
| none | 0 whole months and a part month | 1 |

Where exactly one booked preventive visit stands unanswered and no whole month has yet been completed since the anchor day, the count is one month, because it never falls below one. Where every booked preventive visit has been answered, a part month counts as a whole month in the run from the anchor day to the day the charge is raised.
